readings_ruling: The mark holds. I read the statement against the transcription (l.718–724) and against the scan's page image (journal p. 257 = PDF p. 30, 100 dpi); the scan prints the statement exactly as transcribed. I also read p. 259 = PDF p. 32 (5° and the final step), and it agrees, including the « d'après 4° » flagged [sic]. (1) « variété » read Hausdorff is the standing reading, not an added hypothesis. docs/CAMPAIGN.md (« Benzécri specifics », Implicit hypotheses) gives Benzécri's variété as connected, Hausdorff and second countable unless he says otherwise, and asks only that the reading be recorded under `questions`, which the REPORT does. Plan F6 (campaign/WP-45-plan) says the same. DEC-122 treats « variété » as Hausdorff: its finding against § 2 Prop. 2 is that B need not be Hausdorff, and Structure/Classes.lean:72 cites the reading as ruled under DEC-122. DEC-127 marks rows over connected Hausdorff locally projective manifolds. Marked strict rows carry `[T2Space _]` as « ✓ carried » for « variété »: UniversalCoverRow.lean:57/65 (« as everywhere in the strict library »), Applications/TheoremA.lean:30, Circle.lean:57, Products.lean:71, Converse.lean:44, Cone/*. So `[T2Space V]` is correctly « ✓ carried », not « ⚠ strengthened ». The closer's argued counterexample is correct as stated. Take W an open segment of S(1) with closure in an open hemisphere, h hyperbolic fixing ∂W, and double the orbit D = h^ℤ(m₀). The result is connected and T1, and each copy of W is open and maps homeomorphically by p. h lifts to an automorphism. The compact set (copy 1 of [m₀, h m₀]) ∪ {copy 2 of m₀} generates, the closure of p(V) lies in H̊, and p is not injective. So T2 is also necessary for the Lean statement. (2) « connexe » as Mathlib's ConnectedSpace (nonempty) is DEC-128's « variété is nonempty ». For V = ∅ the conclusion is false, because a chart with source ∅ cannot have the nonempty target int K. (3) « $\overline{p(V)}\subset\mathring H$ » with ⊂ read as ⊆ is Bourbaki's inclusion, as in the T-bz-c2-compact ruling. (4) Sphere.IsOpenHemisphere is Déf. 5 as printed. It admits l = 0, so H = ∅, a harmless weakening of the hypothesis: closure(range p) ⊆ ∅ is impossible for a nonempty V. (5) « projection p sur S(n) compatible avec la structure projective [ouvert étalé] » is IsDeveloping (GSR n) p, the reading of Prop. 1. « sur » cannot mean onto here, because p(V) = S(n) does not fit in a hemisphere. OQ-45 and OQ-62 are independent, checked on the statement and on the proof term. The statement mentions no pseudo-length, pseudo-ball or radius. Its vocabulary is IsCorpsConvexeS, IsCompatibleChart, IsDeveloping, IsBalayable and IsOpenHemisphere, all strict and none touched by either question. In the proof, n = 0 is the branch `subsingleton_dim_zero` + `isCorpsConvexeS_singleton_S0` + `isOpen_singleton_S0`, with no pseudo-length. hasBasis_pseudoBoule is called only under NeZero n. `ouvert_plein` (strict, proved for every r > 0) is called with the r > 0 produced by 2°/3°. Whatever OQ-45 or OQ-62 rules, the marked statement stays true and stays the paper's.

labels.label: bzprop:c2s3p2_hemisphere_corps_convexe
labels.notes: Correctly MARKED. The elaborated type (#check @Benzecri.hemisphere_corps_convexe) is: ∀ {n} {V : Type u} [TopologicalSpace V] [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] [T2Space V] [ConnectedSpace V] {p : V → S n}, IsDeveloping (GSR n) p → IsBalayable (GSR n) (S n) V → ∀ {H}, Sphere.IsOpenHemisphere H → closure (range p) ⊆ H → ∃ K, IsCorpsConvexeS n K ∧ interior K = enveloppeConvexe (range p) ∧ ∃ φ : OpenPartialHomeomorph V (S n), IsCompatibleChart (GSR n) φ ∧ φ.source = univ ∧ φ.target = interior K ∧ ⇑φ = p. Hypothesis by hypothesis against l.718–722: « variété localement projective » is the strict encoding plus T2 (the standing reading, see readings_ruling); second countability is dropped, a weakening. « connexe » is ConnectedSpace. « balayable » is IsBalayable, which is IsBalayableFor ⊤ (Déf. 15, strict). « projection p … compatible » is IsDeveloping. « hémisphère ouvert H̊ » is IsOpenHemisphere. « $\overline{p(V)}\subset\mathring H$ » is closure (range p) ⊆ H. No NeZero n appears, so every dimension is covered. The conclusion « p est une carte de V sur l'intérieur d'un corps convexe de S(n) » is ∃ K a convex body (Déf. 11, strict: strict convex part, compact, nonempty interior) and a compatible chart (Déf. 13, strict: every jet in J(V), equivalently in the maximal atlas) whose underlying map is p, with source all of V and target int K. That is « p est une carte de V sur int K » exactly, not merely « at least ». The extra conjunct interior K = enveloppeConvexe (range p) strengthens the conclusion (Lean ≥ paper). It is meaningful: enveloppeConvexe_isLeast proves that the hull is a convex part (Déf. 8), contains p(V), and lies in every convex part containing p(V), and enveloppeConvexe_subset_hemisphere puts it in H̊. That is l.728's « le plus petit convexe de H̊ contenant p(V) ». The printed form HemisphereCorpsConvexePrinted n (#print) quantifies over V : Type with T2Space, ConnectedSpace and SecondCountableTopology, every developing p, sweepability, and every open hemisphere containing the closure of p(V). Its conclusion is the statement's, without the extra conjunct: word for word the printed proposition. hemisphereCorpsConvexePrinted n is proved for every n as a corollary of the anchor. Proof-level findings: (1) 3° (l.759–762) is a genuine gap of justification. Properties 1°–7° (l.229–259) contain no triangle inequality. Continuity of l_W on W × W with compactness of E does not by itself put the pseudo-balls of one radius centred near p(M) inside the pseudo-ball of 2°: the missing step is the connectedness of pseudo-balls (l.417) plus compactness of a frontier, which is what exists_pos_eventually_pseudoBoule_subset supplies. The statement is unaffected. (2) 2° and 5° use V Hausdorff. Correct: on the line with two origins, the two sections over ℝ meet without being equal. This is not an error of the paper, since « variété » is Hausdorff. (3) The [sic] readings (déf. 5 → déf. 6 at l.750, « d'après 4° » → 3° at l.796) are those flagged in the transcription, and the scan agrees. (4) n = 0 and (5) OQ-62 are checked above. Every line citation (l.229–259, 417, 718–724, 726–800, 746–748, 750, 751–756, 759–762, 764–769, 775–779, 781–796, 786–789, 798–799) was checked against the transcription.
labels.printed_form: Benzecri.HemisphereCorpsConvexePrinted n, proved for every n by Benzecri.hemisphereCorpsConvexePrinted
labels.non_vacuity: The hypotheses are jointly satisfiable in every dimension, and the anchor and the printed form both apply. The audit probe (/tmp/audit-bzhemi/Witness.lean, compiled against the closer's olean, standard axioms, then deleted, about 150 lines) did this for every n: V = corpsInterior A, where A = Sphere.ofCone {v | ∀ i, 0 < v i} is the open simplex of S(n) and is open, so int A = A; p = Subtype.val. IsDeveloping holds by the chart-jet argument of Poches.isDeveloping_val_demiDroiteOuverte. V is connected as the image of the convex orthant and T2 as a subspace. It is swept by the positive diagonal matrices, which act transitively: diag(v) is made an automorphism of V by the file's own autInterior, and the generating compact is the singleton {[1,…,1]}. closure A ⊆ openHemisphere (Σ vᵢ), by Sphere.F_closure and the closed nonnegative orthant. hemisphere_corps_convexe and hemisphereCorpsConvexePrinted n (with SecondCountableTopology (S n) from S.homeomorphEuclideanSphere) were both applied to this data. Neither the file nor the strict library has such a witness for n ≥ 1. For n = 0 a single point already serves. A compact V never works for n ≥ 1: p(V) would be a compact open subset of the connected S(n), so all of S(n), which no hemisphere contains. Hence every witness for n ≥ 1 is non-compact.

lemmas_checked.mem_of_injOn_of_isPreconnected: Correct as stated, and true: X is T2, p is an open map, O and O' are open with p injective on each, B is preconnected and lies under both, and the two sections meet over B. Then every point of O over B lies in O'. Without T2 it is false (line with two origins), as the SCOPE says.
lemmas_checked.simplyConnectedSpace_corpsInterior: Correct: the interior of a convex body of S(n) is homeomorphic, through nrm ℓ, to the convex set F(int K) ∩ {ℓ = 1}, hence contractible.
lemmas_checked.enveloppeConvexe / enveloppeConvexe_isLe: The hull is the set of rays of convexHull F(A). It is the least convex part (Déf. 8, ∪ reading DEC-120) containing A, and it lies in H̊. Its closure is a convex body when A is open and nonempty with closure in H̊: the closed cone {c‖v‖ ≤ l v} contains the closure of the hull, so the hull is strict. All as stated.
lemmas_checked.exists_pos_eventually_pseudoBoule_subset: Correct as stated: [NeZero n] and K a convex body. Every neighbourhood U of m contains the pseudo-balls of one radius s > 0 centred at every point near m.
lemmas_checked.IsFeuille / HasFeuille: A sheet is an open O on which p is injective with p(O) the pseudo-ball of W. That is 2°'s « la restriction de p à O_M soit une carte sur une pseudo-boule » without the intrinsic description of l.746–748, as the SCOPE discloses. These are auxiliary notions of the proof and appear in no marked statement.
lemmas_checked.exists_hasFeuille, exists_hasFeuille_of_: Statements are the paper's 2°, 3° (both paragraphs), 4°, 5° and the final step, each under the hypotheses it actually uses. isCoveringMapOn_interior needs no convex-body hypothesis on K. exists_chart_of_injective is true for any injective developing map. No statement is vacuous or definitionally trivial.
lemmas_checked.autInterior, homeomorphInterior, image_p: γ preserving int K gives a projective automorphism of corpsInterior K (GXAut.ofBijective), which maps pseudo-balls onto pseudo-balls of the same radius. Correct. The audit's witness reuses autInterior.

findings.what: The conclusion row reads « ✓ carried … ; ⚠ strengthened by `interior K = enveloppeConvexe (range p)` », and the REPORT marks the row "strengthened". In kb 0006 (and .claude/agents/lean-auditor.md:40), « ⚠ strengthened » means the Lean theorem assumes more than the paper: an added hypothesis, which is a finding and is incompatible with a mark. Here the Lean proves more, an extra conjunct in the conclusion, which is the harmless direction (Lean ≥ paper). As written, the row tells a reader of the contract that the marked row carries an added hypothesis. The dispatch itself uses « ⚠ strengthened » in that sense. The mark is not affected.
